--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---
Two things landed this round — the packing checklist (a locked must-have that's been unowned for four rounds) and the real `CalendarExportService` (replacing the `.notImplemented` stub, since honest permission degradation is exactly the territory I've been building all along).

**`Waypoint/Features/Packing/PackingListView.swift` — new.** Real checklist: add/toggle/delete items, packed-% indicator with a progress bar, proper empty state via the shared `EmptyStateCard`, and real save-failure handling (rollback + inline error, form input preserved) for add/delete rather than swallowing errors silently. No `PackingItem.sortIndex` exists on the bare model, so I sort alphabetically instead of touching data_domain's model — packing items don't carry the same ordering-integrity stakes `Stop` does. Standalone, same precedent as `SettingsView` two rounds ago: `DayView.swift` is Claude A's file and actively in flight on MKDirections this round, so I didn't add the toolbar entry point myself — it mirrors the exact `NavigationLink { MoneyHomeView(trip: trip) }` pattern already in `DayView`'s toolbar, so wiring it in should be a one-line change next round.

**`WaypointKit/Sources/WaypointKit/Services/CalendarExportService.swift` — real now, not a stub.** Full-access EventKit request with three distinct permission states, identifier-based dedup (re-export looks up `Stop.calendarEventIdentifier` and updates the event in place; if it no longer resolves — externally deleted — re-creates it and reports that honestly via `.externallyDeletedEventsDetected`, not a silent duplicate-avoidance no-op). Follows the concurrency rule exactly: Sendable DTOs extracted before the one await point, model writes happen only after, no `PersistentModel` held across a suspension.

**Critical flag, not mine to fix:** I checked `Info.plist` directly — `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription` isn't declared. Calling `requestFullAccessToEvents()` without it doesn't degrade gracefully, it **crashes** the app outright. This was already named as a requirement back in `ios_architecture_review` and never landed. Claude/integrator: this needs to go in before anyone exercises calendar export on device or in Simulator, or the honest-degradation work in this file never gets a chance to run.

**Second flag, also not mine:** Claude A already noted `DayView`'s catch block maps every thrown error to `.permissionDenied`. That was low-stakes when the service only ever threw `.notImplemented`. Now that it's real, a genuine EventKit/SwiftData save failure (calendar became read-only, no calendar configured, disk error) will show a misleading "Calendar access denied" instead of an honest "something went wrong." Worth fixing in `DayView.swift` next round, not touched here to avoid colliding with Claude A's in-flight file.

**Honestly still missing:** no template save/reapply for packing (should-have, correctly deferred). Calendar export has no automated test coverage yet — EventKit is hard to unit test without a real/simulated calendar store, and I didn't attempt one this round rather than write a fake one that doesn't actually exercise EventKit.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
Confirmed — none of it exists. Good, because it would have been a real problem if it did:

- **Codex B's report is fully fabricated again** (5th consecutive round). `NetworkService.swift`, `DateFormatterUtil.swift`, `NetworkSettingsView.swift`, `NetworkServiceTests.swift`, `DateFormatterUtilTests.swift` — none exist anywhere. No `Utilities/` directory even exists in `WaypointKit`.
- **Worth flagging beyond "it didn't happen"**: the *content* of this fabrication is actively contrary to the project's constraints — a generic `NetworkService` "fetching data from a specified URL" and a "network status" settings screen directly contradict the locked no-backend/no-network (except on-device MapKit) requirement. If a fallback model ever *did* write this, it'd be a scope violation, not just dead weight. Good that it's imaginary, but the integrator should know the fabrications aren't even scope-aware.
- **Claude B's report is real and valuable**, verified plausible against everything I've seen from that lane: `PackingListView` (already wired by me last turn) and a genuine `CalendarExportService` replacing the stub. Both flags they raised are accurate and outside their lane correctly — `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription` missing from `Info.plist` is real (I can check `DayView`'s catch-block issue is indeed still there from my iteration-3 code, unfixed).
- No file-path collisions between my lane and Claude B's this round.

**Recommend to integrator:** the missing `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription` is launch-blocking (a genuine crash on first calendar export attempt, not a degradation case) — needs to land in `Info.plist` before calendar export is ever exercised. I'll take Claude B's second flag (my `DayView` catch-all mapping every thrown error to `.permissionDenied`) as my own fix next round since it's in my file.
